Every FanDuel leg on the slate

Model %
How often the BetSweep model expects this leg to hit, after adjusting for the player's own history at that line.
Book %
How often it has to hit for FanDuel's price to break even. −110 means 52.4%; +200 means 33.3%. The book builds its margin in here.
Edge
Model % minus Book %, in percentage points. +7.0 means the model thinks the leg hits 7 points more often than the price requires — you're being paid more than the risk deserves. Negative means FanDuel is charging more than the leg is worth. Rough guide from the model's own verdicts: +2 and up is value, +5 and up is strong value, between −2 and +2 is a fair price, below −2 is a pass. Edge is the main sort because it's the number that makes money over time, not the hit rate on its own.
Fair
The odds the model would set for the whole slip. If FanDuel's price is longer than fair, the parlay has edge; the "take it at … or better" line leaves a 5% cushion for line movement.
EV per $1
Expected profit per dollar staked if the model is right: model hit chance × payout − 1. Positive is good; it is an average over many bets, not a promise on this one.
Last 5 dots
Did he clear the selected line in each of his last five games, newest first. Tap for the full panel and what the defense has allowed.

      Model % is the model's history-adjusted hit rate for that line; book % is what FanDuel's price implies; edge is the difference in points (positive = the price pays more than the risk deserves). "Fair" prices the whole combination: legs from different games are independent, legs from the same game are linked with the model's correlations (receptions ↔ receiving yards, QB ↔ his receivers, and so on).
